character.actionsDesc: For routine editing, work directly in the character asset workspace below.
character.addDialogDesc: Open this only when creating a new character or importing from the base character library. For routine maintenance, use the character asset workspace directly.
character.autoCompleteProfile: Auto-complete personality, background, growth arc, and current state
character.heroDesc: First check whether the character lineup can support the main storyline, then maintain the current character assets; add, import, and supplement as phase actions when needed.
character.importFromLibraryDesc: Good for quickly bringing in mature templates, then fine-tuning to the current novel's needs.
character.libraryEmpty: The base character library is empty. Please create one first.
character.quickCreateDesc: Good for quickly adding a new character placeholder, then refining it in the workspace below.
character.stat.coreDesc: At least define the protagonist and the main antagonist.
character.stat.createdDesc: First fill in placeholders for the characters that drive the main storyline.
character.storyFunctionPlaceholder: Role in the story (e.g., drives the truth thread)
character.supplemental.analyzing: Analyzing the current character network and generating candidates...
character.supplemental.applied: {{name}} has been added to the current novel.
character.supplemental.appliedWithRelati: {{name}} has been added to the current novel, with {{count}} relations synced.
character.supplemental.applyFailed: Failed to apply the supplemental character.
character.supplemental.countAutoBadge: When count is left unset, AI decides
character.supplemental.dialogDesc: Good for adding a missing character on top of an existing character system. You can specify "derive from existing relations" or "generate a relatively independent character", or let AI decide.
character.supplemental.emptyHint: Describe what kind of character you want to add, or let AI decide, then generate candidates.
character.supplemental.extraNotesPlaceho: For example: I want someone who keeps pressuring the protagonist but is not a pure villain; or an old acquaintance tied to the mother thread.
character.supplemental.independentNote: This character leans toward an independent addition; relations are not forced in.
character.supplemental.modeHint: "AI decides" is recommended by default; specify manually only when you are sure which kind of character to add.
character.supplemental.modeOption.auto: Let AI decide which kind of supplement is needed now
character.supplemental.modeOption.linked: Derive a related character from existing characters
character.supplemental.noCharactersForLi: There are no created characters yet, so a relationship-based supplement is not possible. Create a core character first, or switch to "generate a relatively independent character".
character.supplemental.referenceHint: Optional; if none is selected, AI decides on its own who to build around.
character.supplemental.relationBadge: Related characters are added around existing characters first
character.supplemental.useWorldContext: Generate based on this book's world
character.takeoverDesc: AI first judges whether the character assets are complete, then decides whether to keep adding characters or rerun the current step as you choose.
editView.defaultDescription: Organize this book's production assets by the current step; hand off to the AI auto-director when needed.
editView.devToolsResetNote: After reset, all chapter drafts, fact ledgers, summaries, and quality reports are cleared, and chapter status returns to "not planned". Planning-layer data (characters, outline, volume plans) stays unchanged.
editView.exportDialogDesc: The current step exports the workbench you are viewing; the whole book exports project settings, story planning, characters, volume plans, chapter breakdowns, chapters, and quality-repair assets together.
editView.projectToolsDesc: Secondary information is collected here. The first screen keeps only the current step and the resume-takeover entry, to avoid cluttering the main workspace with auxiliary project info.
editView.resetConfirm: Reset all {{count}} chapter drafts of this novel? This cannot be undone (but snapshot data is kept).
editView.resetError: Chapter reset failed. Please try again.
editView.resetSuccess: Reset {{count}} chapter drafts. You can regenerate them.
editView.workflowRecommend: Workflow suggestion: switch to "{{value}}" to continue.
outline.canContinueStage: You can continue advancing this stage.
outline.derivedTextDesc: This part leans toward wrap-up and comparison; it is not something you must keep watching while editing the current volume skeleton.
outline.derivedTextTitle: Derived text, version control, and impact analysis
outline.diffStats: Changed volumes {{volumes}} | affected chapters {{chapters}} | changed lines {{lines}}
outline.field.title: Volume title
outline.goToBeatEdit: Go to beats / chapter split to edit the curve
outline.impactStats: Affected volumes {{volumes}} | affected chapters {{chapters}} | changed lines {{lines}}
outline.nextAction.beatThenChapters: Do the current volume's beat sheet first, then split its chapters
outline.nextAction.generateSkeleton: Now is a good time to generate the whole-book volume skeleton
outline.nextAction.ready: The volume-strategy stage is complete; you can proceed to beats / chapter split
outline.nextAction.toBeat: The volume skeleton is ready; next go to beats / chapter split
outline.noResourceCommitment: This volume has no character-resource commitments to watch closely.
outline.noSkeletonHint: There is no volume skeleton yet. Generate a volume-strategy suggestion first, then click "Generate whole-book volume skeleton".
outline.noStrategyHint: There is no volume-strategy suggestion yet. Click "Generate volume-strategy suggestion" first.
outline.noVersions: No volume versions yet; save a draft version first.
outline.openPayoffsPlaceholder: One per line, or separated by commas.
outline.readiness.beatSheet.desc: Only after the volume skeleton is stable should you move into per-volume beat splitting.
outline.readiness.beatSheet.label: Beat sheet
outline.readiness.chapterList.desc: Only after the beat sheet is ready can you continue splitting down to the chapter level.
outline.readiness.chapterList.label: Split chapters
outline.readiness.skeleton.desc: Confirm each volume's opening hook, pressure source, and payoff method.
outline.readiness.skeleton.label: Volume skeleton
outline.readiness.strategy.desc: First get the recommended volume count, hard/soft planning, and escalation ladder.
outline.readiness.strategy.label: Volume strategy
outline.resourceCommitmentDesc: Shows only resources that affect this volume's action boundaries, setups, or later payoffs.
outline.resourceCommitmentTitle: Key resource commitments for this volume
outline.resourceWindow.expected: Expected to be used from chapter {{start}} to chapter {{end}}
outline.selectVolumeHint: Select a volume on the left, or generate the whole-book skeleton first, then edit the current volume's details here.
outline.stageFullyReady: The current volume-strategy stage has full conditions to proceed.
outline.standardVolumeScale: The standard volume scale is designed at {{min}}-{{max}} chapters per volume, with an ideal of about {{ideal}} chapters per volume. Very long books add more volumes by default to preserve each volume's sense of stage, escalation nodes, and volume-level payoff, rather than compressing into a few huge volumes.
outline.strategySkeletonDesc: First let the system decide the volume count and hard/soft planning, then confirm a volume skeleton that can proceed to beat-sheet splitting.
outline.strategySummaryDesc: Look at the whole book's volume-level payoffs and escalation path first, then pick a volume below for detailed editing.
outline.suggestAddCharacters: It is recommended to add characters first, then generate the volume strategy and skeleton.
outline.suggestImpactAnalysis: It is recommended to run volume-level impact analysis before activating.
outline.takeoverDesc: AI first judges whether the volume strategy and skeleton are complete, then decides whether to fill in what is missing or rerun the current step.
outline.volumeCountMode.system: Currently using the system's suggested {{count}} volumes
outline.volumeCountReviewDesc: This is supporting decision info. Look at the recommended next step and current volume first; expand review and volume-count control only when needed.
outline.volumeNavDesc: Use the volume title and description on the left to locate the volume you want to edit.
outline.volumeNavFallback: Fill in this volume's title and description first for easier navigation later.
outline.volumeTensionSubtitle: View the chapter conflict-intensity trend; red dots mark the intensity you have pinned for the AI to keep later.
outline.workspaceReady: The current workspace already has the basic conditions to continue.
pipeline.bibleWorldRecordDesc: This is the written record in the story bible; chapter generation reads the world handbook and usage scope from "this book's world" first.
pipeline.configSummaryDesc: Batch tasks, models, and advanced parameters are all collected here. By default, handle the current problem chapter first, and expand this only when you need to push forward in bulk.
pipeline.configSummaryTitle: Pipeline config, run, and model settings
pipeline.lowScoreRange: {{count}} low-score chapters; rerun range: chapter {{start}} - chapter {{end}}.
pipeline.needCharacter: Add at least 1 character before running the pipeline.
pipeline.noBelowThreshold: No chapters currently below the threshold.
pipeline.noObviousLowScore: No obvious low-score chapters right now
pipeline.noRunningJob: No pipeline task is currently running.
pipeline.reportSummaryDesc: Full quality reports, the saved bible, and beats are all view-only info and are collapsed by default.
pipeline.takeoverDesc: AI first checks whether there is an active chapter batch or a pending-repair checkpoint, then decides whether to resume the current repair or start a new batch.
resourceRecommend.appliedMessage: The AI-recommended genre base and story mode have been filled into the current form. You can keep fine-tuning, or go straight to AI auto-director.
resourceRecommend.error: AI failed to recommend a resource set. Please try again later.
resourceRecommend.leadDesc: You do not need to understand the genre base library or story-mode library first. Just write one line of inspiration, a selling point, or a first-30-chapter promise, and the system will recommend a default set better suited for beginners.
resourceRecommend.leadTitle: Let AI recommend a starting foundation first
resourceRecommend.noContextHint: Add at least one of inspiration, synopsis, target audience, selling point, or first-30-chapter promise, so AI can more reliably judge which genre and story mode you should start from.
resourceRecommend.noSecondaryMode: For now it is better to stabilize the primary story mode first; stacking too many flavors at the start is not recommended.
resourceRecommend.staleHint: You just changed the setup info. It is recommended to run the recommendation again so the genre and story mode keep up with the latest direction.
style.appliedMessage: This style is now the book's default. The first half of the auto-director reads only a lightweight summary; the full rules kick back in during content planning and generation.
style.bindError: Style binding failed. Please try again later.
style.cardDesc: This is where you pick and apply the book-level writing style for the current novel. Style assets belong to the resource layer and should be consumed here by the novel, rather than the asset library deciding in reverse which book uses it.
style.contentPhase: Content phase: once bound, the planner and runtime keep using the full style rules and anti-AI constraints.
style.emptyResultHint: This area shows 2-3 style options the system picked for the current novel, and explains why they fit and what to watch out for.
style.noAssetsHint: There are no recommendable style assets yet. Build 1-2 in the style engine first, then come back to choose one for this book.
style.noBindingHint: This book has no default style bound yet. It is recommended to let the system suggest 2-3 candidates based on the current novel's target audience, selling points, and first-30-chapter promise.
style.planningPhase: Planning phase: the auto-director and chapter planning read only the reading-experience promise / language density / dialogue style / emotional expression / anti-AI summary.
style.recommendError: Style recommendation failed. Please try again later.
style.setAsDefault: Set as this book's default style
takeoverDialog.description: It reads the current project's real progress first, then tells you clearly which steps will be skipped, continued, or rerun this time.
takeoverDialog.fullBookDesc: The system takes over the current project targeting the whole book, continuing planning, chapter execution, review, and repair. It stops only for an unavailable model, service error, content protection, or unrecoverable risk.
takeoverDialog.hasActiveTaskDesc: To avoid a duplicate takeover, handle the current auto-director task first.
takeoverDialog.postReviewDesc: When enabled, after chapter content is generated it checks for AI-flavor risk and produces a revised draft when a fixable issue is found.
takeoverDialog.runModeOption.byRange.des: Take over by whole book, chapter range, or volume range, and keep preparing chapter execution for the target range.
takeoverDialog.runModeOption.fullBook.de: AI fills in planning, keeps writing, reviews, and repairs toward the whole-book goal.
takeoverDialog.runModeOption.toReady.des: AI keeps advancing until chapter-execution resources are ready, then hands off.
takeoverDialog.scopeNotAllowed: The current range cannot start from this step. A chapter range starts from beat-based chapter split; a volume range starts from volume strategy.
takeoverDialog.stageStyleSummary: Style summary effective only this stage: {{value}}
takeoverDialog.startFailedNoTask: Failed to start auto-director; no task info returned.
takeoverDialog.strategyOption.continue.d: Skip completed assets first, filling only what is missing or resuming the current batch.
takeoverDialog.strategyOption.restart.de: Clear the current step's output first, then regenerate it for that step.
takeoverDialog.styleKeywordsOnly: Reuse only the style keywords for now
takeoverDialog.styleSection: Writing style used for this takeover
takeoverDialog.styleSectionDesc: After binding a book-level default style, it is recommended to reuse it during takeover. The first half of directing reads only a lightweight summary to avoid interfering with structural planning.
takeoverDialog.submittedFullBook: The auto-director takeover task has been submitted; you can view whole-book execution progress in the AI cockpit.
takeoverDialog.submittedQueued: The auto-director takeover task has been submitted; you can view queue and execution progress in the AI cockpit.
takeoverDialog.submittedRange: The auto-director takeover task has been submitted; you can view execution progress for {{label}} in the AI cockpit.
takeoverDialog.title: Let AI continue auto-directing from the current project
takeoverVm.assetProgressIntro: Below is the asset progress detected for the current project.
takeoverVm.card.chapterDetailReady: {{count}} chapter task sheets / execution resources prepared.
takeoverVm.card.noExecutableRange: No executable chapter range detected yet.
takeoverVm.card.notStartedContent: Content production has not started yet.
takeoverVm.card.volumePlanDetail: {{volumes}} volumes; current volume {{chapters}} chapters; split ranges {{ranges}}
takeoverVm.continueFromTo: Start at chapter {{start}} and advance continuously to chapter {{end}}.
takeoverVm.error.existingTask: An auto-director task is already handling this book. Enter and continue the current task first, or cancel it before taking over.
takeoverVm.error.notInChapterStage: This project has not entered the chapter production stage yet, so you cannot continue directly from a chapter range. It is recommended to continue from the system-recommended position.
takeoverVm.guidance.canContinueAfterRead: You can continue once reading finishes.
takeoverVm.guidance.canResumeFrom: The system detects the project can resume from "{{label}}".
takeoverVm.guidance.chapterNearOrder: The system detects chapter execution has reached around chapter {{order}}; it is recommended to return to the current task and continue first.
takeoverVm.guidance.existingTaskStopped: A director task is already stopped at "{{stage}}".
takeoverVm.guidance.keepAssetsDefault: Existing writing assets are kept by default.
takeoverVm.guidance.noDuplicateTakeover: Continuing the current task will not start a duplicate takeover.
takeoverVm.guidance.readingProgress: Reading project progress; a recommended resume position will be given once reading finishes.
takeoverVm.protection.keepChapters: Keep the existing {{count}} chapters of content or chapter assets.
takeoverVm.protection.keepVolumes: Reuse existing volume-plan assets and fill only later gaps.
takeoverVm.protection.noCharacters: No created characters detected; AI will complete character prep.
takeoverVm.protection.noVolumes: No volume plan detected; AI will keep generating the volume plan.
takeoverVm.runModeAction.fullBookAutopil: Take over the whole book and advance
taskDrawer.confirmForWriting: Confirm and use for later writing
taskDrawer.description: View this book's AI progress records, quick actions, and troubleshooting info.
taskDrawer.moreResourceChanges: {{count}} more resource changes; you can keep handling them in the relevant chapters.
taskDrawer.noActionNeeded: No AI progress action needs handling right now.
taskDrawer.noMilestones: No milestone records to show yet.
taskDrawer.noQuickActions: No quick actions available to run right now.
taskDrawer.noTokenUsage: This task has no displayable token usage yet; once the model starts returning usage, this refreshes automatically.
taskDrawer.noVisibleTask: This novel has no visible auto-director task yet. You can keep writing manually, or check other tasks in the background task center.
taskDrawer.resourceChangeDesc: These decisions affect which key resources later chapters can use.
workflowIndicator.defaultLabel: AI keeps advancing in the background
worldManager.chainHasSlice: Characters, outline, and chapters inherit the rules, forces, and locations in this book's usage scope first.
worldManager.chainNoSlice: After organizing this book's usage scope, the generation chain reads more precise world constraints.
worldManager.chainReadsWorld: The generation chain reads this world
worldManager.chapterReadsScope: Chapter generation reads this book's usage scope.
worldManager.constraintPlaceholder: After creating this book's world, the constraints chapter generation will read appear here.
worldManager.selectOrGenerate: Select or generate this book's world
worldManager.selectOrGenerateDesc: Import from the world library, generate from this book, or create a custom world skeleton first.
worldManager.summaryNoWorld: First create a world copy for this book; later characters, outline, and chapters will all read the setting boundaries here.
worldManager.summaryOrganizing: This book's world is being organized.
worldManager.writingStatus.needsOrganize: Needs organizing this book's usable scope
worldUsage.bookWorldDetail: Chapter generation reads this book's world copy.
worldUsage.boundaryPlaceholder: After organizing, this book's usage boundary will be generated.
worldUsage.detailsDesc: Here you confirm the rules, forces, and locations that chapter generation actually reads. You can specify only a few must-keep items and let the system trim the rest to the book's direction.
worldUsage.detailsDisclosureDesc: View and adjust the world constraints this book must keep early on.
worldUsage.manualRetainedDesc: Here you specify only a few items that must appear or must be followed; you do not need to re-enter the whole world.
worldUsage.mustRetainDesc: Good for the opening location, key allies, main enemies, and power costs that cannot be broken.
worldUsage.mustRetainForcesDesc: Forces you cannot miss early on, such as the protagonist's origin, main enemies, and key allies.
worldUsage.mustRetainLocationsDesc: The opening location, trial grounds, conflict flashpoints, and stages readers need to remember repeatedly.
worldUsage.mustRetainRulesDesc: Power costs, identity taboos, and boundaries the plot cannot casually break.
worldUsage.mustRetainTitle: Organizations, locations, and rules to keep
worldUsage.noForcesAvailable: No selectable organizations in this book's world yet.
worldUsage.noLocationsAvailable: No selectable locations in this book's world yet.
worldUsage.noRulesAvailable: No selectable rules in this book's world yet.
worldUsage.noSliceHint: This book has not organized the world scope the current story will use yet. After clicking "organize this book's usage scope", a confirmable set of rules, forces, and locations is generated from this book's world and story idea.
worldUsage.noWorldHint: This novel has no book world yet. Import one from the world library, or generate a world based on this book's theme, then organize the rules, forces, and locations the current story mainly uses.
worldUsage.scopeNoteDesc: You can add a boundary line, for example "keep the realistic urban base, do not turn it into a fantasy power-leveling story".
worldUsage.scopeNoteLabel: Early-stage boundary note not to cross
worldUsage.scopeNotePlaceholder: For example: keep the original realistic business environment and character pressure; do not introduce a supernatural system.
worldUsage.storyInputSource.explicit: From the story idea you entered manually this time
worldUsage.storyInputSource.storyMacro: From the story idea in the macro plan
worldUsage.storyInputSourceDetail: The usage scope is trimmed to the current story direction.
worldUsage.summaryHasSlice: These rules, forces, and locations enter character, outline, and chapter generation first.
worldUsage.summaryHasWorld: First organize the world scope this book actually uses, to avoid chapter generation reading too many irrelevant settings.
worldUsage.summaryNoWorld: First create or import this book's world, then organize the scope that generation will read.
